ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is square ABCD, with A at the lower left, B at the upper left, C at the upper right, and D at the lower right. Point M is on the bottom side AD, and point N is on the right side CD. The segments AN, BN, BM, and CM are drawn in the figure. It can be read from the figure: triangle ABN is exactly composed of regions S7, S8, and S3; triangle ABM is composed of S7 and S6; triangle CDM is composed of S2, S3, and S4. Reasoning: Because ABCD is a square, and M is on AD, the sum of the horizontal distances from point M to AB and to CD is equal to the side length of the square. Therefore, calculating with AB and CD as bases, the sum of the areas of triangle ABM and triangle CDM is equal to half of the area of the square. Also because N is on CD, triangle ABN has AB as its base, and its height is equal to the side length of the square, so the area of triangle ABN is also half of the area of the square. Therefore [ABN]=[ABM]+[CDM]. Substituting the area decomposition in the figure: S7+S8+S3=(S7+S6)+(S2+S3+S4). Eliminating S7 and S3 from both sides gives S8=S2+S4+S6.

method.method_draft: Use a pure area-decomposition argument. From the diagram, identify the drawn segments as AN, BN, BM, and CM. Read off that triangle ABN is exactly the union of regions S7, S8, and S3. Also read off that triangle ABM is the union of S7 and S6, while triangle CDM is the union of S2, S3, and S4. Since ABCD is a square and M lies on AD, the perpendicular distances from M to AB and CD add to the side length, so [ABM] + [CDM] = one half of the square. Also [ABN] is one half of the square because base AB is a side of the square and N lies on the opposite side DC. Therefore [ABN] = [ABM] + [CDM]. Substituting the visible decompositions gives S7 + S8 + S3 = (S7 + S6) + (S2 + S3 + S4), and cancelling S7 and S3 yields S8 = S2 + S4 + S6.
